sources.note: Occupied by Suvorov's Russian and Austrian forces 27 April 1799; the Austrians depart 30 May 1800; restored 2 or 4 June 1800; Adige frontier at Luneville.

sources.title: Subalpine Republic
sources.note: Conquered by Austro-Russian troops 20 June 1799; Piedmontese Republic re-established 20 June 1800.

sources.title: German mediatisation
sources.note: Final Recess of 25 February 1803; table lists a Duke of Breisgau-Modena, an Archduke of Austria (Brixen, Trent); silent on the Breisgau as Austrian and on Ortenau.

sources.title: Duchy of Modena and Reggio
sources.note: Francesco III backed France in 1740, was expelled by Habsburg forces (undated), duchy restored by the 1748 Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle.

sources.title: Treaty of Senlis
sources.note: Signed at Senlis on 23 May 1493: the County of Burgundy, Artois, Charolais and Noyers returned to the Habsburgs (Philip the Handsome); Hesdin, Aire and Bethune stay French.

sources.title: Frederick V, Elector Palatine
sources.note: Bohemian Confederacy formed at Prague on 31 July 1619; Frederick elected 26 August, crowned 4 November 1619; White Mountain 8 November 1620; leaves Silesia in early 1621.

sources.title: Battle of Turin
sources.note: 7 September 1706; Convention of Milan March 1707 (Milan and Mantua handed to Austria); Joseph captures Naples in April (1707 implied).

sources.title: Duchy of Mantua
sources.note: Infobox: Gonzaga rule ends, partitioned and ruled by the Austrian Habsburgs, 1708; Napoleon 1797.

sources.title: State of the Presidi
sources.note: Austrian possession from 1708 (conquered 1708-1712 save Porto Longone); conquered by a Spanish and allied army in May 1735; ceded by diploma 11 December 1736; Peace of Vienna 18 November 1738.

sources.title: Charles VII, Holy Roman Emperor
sources.note: Coronation 12 February 1742; Bavaria occupied by the troops of Maria Theresa; Charles regains Munich in October 1744.

sources.title: Free County of Burgundy
sources.note: Opened by fx-20: the county returned to Philip at Senlis in 1493; in 1512 it was administered as part of the Habsburg Netherlands; Charles king of Spain 1516; never annexed into the Kingdom of Spain.

sources.title: Spanish Netherlands
sources.note: Opened by fx-20: 'held in personal union by the Spanish Habsburgs, but not annexed to the Spanish Crown'; Franche-Comte a separate possession.

sources.title: Kingdom of Bohemia
sources.note: Opened by fx-20: Ferdinand elected king of Bohemia by the Diet; infobox 'Crown land of the Habsburg monarchy (1526-1804)'; 16 December 1526.
